findings: S7 incomplete implementation: The WorkOrder model has identity_reference, identity_traits, and deliverable_set fields with path validation (COMPLETE). The docs/QUALITY_CHARTER.md documents the same-subject test requirement at lines 93-103 (COMPLETE). However, the reviewer-design PROMPT.md does not document the same-subject test duty that S7 requires reviewer-design to perform. The packet_quality_charter_section function injects only the observable criteria, not the full charter text with station duties. A reviewer receiving a work order with identity_reference and deliverable_set would not know from the packet or prompt that a same-subject test is required. The fixture tests in test_quality_standard.py verify the expected review structure but no integration test proves reviewer-design actually produces same_subject_test reviews.

Parsing integrity test carve-out judgment (explicitly requested): HONEST RECONCILIATION. The test_review_parsing_integrity.py test at lines 663-702 carves out reviewer-design and reviewer-ux from the identity requirement for Output Format sections. This reconciles two legitimately conflicting contracts: wo-gh-16 requires identical Output Format sections across all reviewers; wo-gh-15 S1 requires reviewer-design and reviewer-ux to have dual-section structure for quality judgments. The carve-out maintains wo-gh-16 for the 7 standard reviewers (enforcing identical formats) while allowing the 2 visual reviewers their required extension. The carve-out is documented with its reason in the test code. This is the correct resolution when two specs genuinely conflict on scope.
